title: Verdance Tech - hosting & crypto ops intake
topics: hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment
summary: Intro discovery focused on security gating for production inference. Customer leans toward private deployment due to data residency and regulatory auditing; exploring KMS options and RBAC model. Redwood AE/SE clarified hosted/dedicated tradeoffs, SOC2 evidence, SAML SSO flow, and audit log retention. Agreed to share SOC2 report, KMS integration diagram, and a short pilot proposal + benchmark recipe.
next_steps: Alex to share SOC2 + ISO attestation and security deck by 2026-06-04
Priya to propose a pilot bench plan and private deployment checklist by 2026-06-08
Verdance to confirm timeline for legal review (Nadia)
action_items: Alex Martinez: send SOC2 report + redwood-security-deck.pdf link (due 2026-06-04)
Priya Shah: draft pilot benchmark recipe and expected metrics (due 2026-06-08)
Sam Ortiz: provide list of data classes and retention requirements (due 2026-06-07)
Leah Park: confirm preferred VPC region and egress controls (due 2026-06-06)
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-06-02 16:00 UTC | Duration: 48m | Attendees: Alex Martinez, Priya Shah, Dana Liu (Redwood) — Markus Engel, Leah Park, Sam Ortiz, Nadia (Verdance)

[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Um, quick roll call — I'm Alex, AE on the account, Priya our SE is here, Dana's on to help with onboarding and the billing bits.
[00:14] Markus (Verdance - VP Eng): Hey Alex, thanks. Markus here. Leah and Sam with me — Nadia's on for legal.
[00:25] Alex: Great. High level — we want to understand your security gating, deployment preference, and where you've got hard constraints. Start with you, Markus, high level ask?
[00:40] Markus: Sure, yeah. We're evaluating inference platforms for product features that touch PII and customer payment metadata. Our legal and audit teams need strong encryption at rest/in transit, KMS integration with our HSM, and auditable trails. Ideally something that fits within our VPC for production.
[00:55] Priya (Redwood SE): Thanks. When you say "fits within our VPC" — are you thinking an on-prem private control plane or Redwood Private (VPC peering / private deployment)?
[01:08] Leah: Prefer Redwood Private in our cloud account; we want control over network egress and no multitenant peek. Also SSO must be SAML with SCIM for provisioning.
[01:20] Sam (Security): And we need full audit logs for model calls, with 12 month retention, plus immutable logs where possible.
[01:33] Alex: Understood. So main buckets — identity (SSO/SCIM/RBAC), encryption/KMS, audit logs/retention, and compliance artifacts (SOC2/ISO).
[01:45] Nadia (Legal): On SOC2 — we need to see the latest Type II report and any exceptions. Also, data processing addendum and subprocessors list.
[01:58] Priya: We'll share SOC2 Type II and ISO attestation. For subprocessors, we maintain a list and can provide contract-level protections.
[02:10] Markus: Ok. Can you describe the KMS story for Private — do we bring our own KMS, or do you manage keys?
[02:22] Priya: For Redwood Private we support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS, GCP KMS, or on-prem HSM. You can either rotate keys from your KMS or we can integrate with a proxy HSM. We also support envelope encryption — model artifacts and cache can be encrypted with customer keys.
[02:40] Leah: Envelope encryption — does that include KV cache and token cache? We can't have unencrypted caches leaving our control.
[02:51] Priya: Yes, KV cache and persistent caches can be encrypted with your customer key. There are a couple of caveats: in-host memory caches are ephemeral but disk-backed caches use envelope encryption. We'll document the exact paths.
[03:08] Alex: Quick practical tradeoff: hosted gives fastest time to value but less key control; dedicated can isolate compute but often still uses Redwood-managed KMS unless you opt for private.
[03:22] Markus: So for production we likely need private. What does the onboarding timeline look like?
[03:30] Dana (Redwood CSM): Typical private onboarding is 4–8 weeks depending on infra approvals and legal. We do a prep checklist first — VPC peering, IAM role creation, KMS policy, and certificate exchange.
[03:47] [Small crosstalk, background noise]
[03:55] Sam: On RBAC — we use least privilege and want role mappings from SAML to roles in the platform. Does Redwood support fine-grained RBAC and audit for role changes?
[04:09] Priya: Yes, we support SAML attribute mapping to groups and roles. You can set least-privilege roles per route/model. All role changes are captured in our admin audit logs with user, time, and action.
[04:22] Sam: Are the admin logs exportable to our SIEM?
[04:27] Priya: Yes, we can stream logs to your CloudWatch/EventHub/Splunk via a sidecar or use S3 export. For Private deployments we can push directly into your logging pipeline.
[04:39] Leah: Retention — we want 12 months of request-level logs and 7 years of access-control changes. Is that configurable?
[04:51] Alex: We support configurable retention windows; for hosted there's standard tiers, but in Private you control retention via your storage. We can set policies to retain the first 12 months for request logs and archive longer-term events. There are cost implications for long retention.
[05:10] Markus: Understood. What about model provenance and versioning? We need to show which model was used for a given inference when audited.
[05:19] Priya: Every inference has metadata — model id, runtime, quantization profile, token counts, and model hash. That gets stored in the request log. We can tie that to your internal ticket/reference.
[05:33] [00:05 seconds pause]
[05:40] Nadia: On legal again — do you sign data processing addenda and what are your retention default policies for customer data?
[05:49] Alex: We have a standard DPA and a model data policy; for Hosted the default is 30 days for request payloads before deletion unless otherwise contracted. For Private you control retention. We'll share the DPA PDF.
[06:03] Sam: Do you do any training on customer data or keep persistent copies for model fine-tuning?
[06:10] Priya: We do not incorporate customer data into our shared models unless explicitly contracted as a separate service. Hosted analytics for quality are aggregated and customer-id stripped, but we'll get that in writing.
[06:25] Markus: Good. On SAML/SCIM — we need SCIM provisioning for service accounts and human users. Can Redwood scope service accounts differently?
[06:35] Priya: Yes, you can have machine principals and human principals. SCIM can provision groups and we support service account tokens with restricted scopes.
[06:44] Leah: And MFA enforcement for admin? We enforce okta/mfa at the idp, but admin console should block changes without MFA.
[06:55] Alex: We honor the IdP MFA signals and can set conditional access requirements. Additionally, privileged operations require two-person approval in some Dedicated/Private plans.
[07:10] [08:00 timestamping jump — call moves into deeper technical lane]
[07:15] Priya: Technical note — for Private, network egress can be disabled at the host level so keys never leave the VPC. We'll send a diagram showing control plane and data plane separation.
[07:28] Sam: Diagram please. Also, do you support VPC endpoints for zero public egress?
[07:35] Priya: Yes, VPC endpoint patterns are supported — we have templates for AWS and GCP. The private control plane still needs an initial handshake during onboarding.
[07:47] Markus: How do you handle failover? If a AZ goes down, do we have a fallback region and how does key access work across regions?
[07:58] Priya: You can replicate keys across regions with KMS multi-region keys or use cross-region replication; that requires key policy adjustments. Automated failover is supported but must be configured in the deployment plan.
[08:12] Leah: On audit items — we need cryptographic proof that logs are tamper-evident. Any support for signed logs or write-once storage?
[08:22] Priya: We can integrate with WORM storage for long-term retention and produce signed log bundles. For high-assurance customers we can produce SHA digests of daily bundles and share via a signed manifest.
[08:36] Sam: That helps. Are there documented SOC2 controls we map to? We have internal control owners and want to map Redwood controls to our matrix.
[08:45] Alex: We'll provide a controls matrix mapping SOC2/ISO clauses to Redwood processes — that's part of the security pack.
[08:55] Nadia: Also need subprocessors list and code provenance — do you have SBOM or dependency lists?
[09:03] Priya: We can provide a software bill of materials for the runtime and major dependencies. For third-party models we provide provenance notes where available.
[09:16] Markus: One sticky point — we have egress limitations due to GAAP data rules. Does Redwood ever send telemetry to third parties for model improvement?
[09:27] Alex: By default we collect telemetry for platform health but it can be disabled in Private. For Hosted we have opt-in for data used in model improvement. We'll capture this in the DPA.
[09:40] [Short pause]
[09:45] Leah: Pricing question quick — private has a setup fee and monthly infra usage; do you have ballpark numbers for committed Dedicated vs Private?
[09:55] Dana: We'll follow up with a tailored estimate; roughly private setup varies by infra footprint but expect a three-figure K setup for onboarding plus ongoing infra costs. We'll put a formal proposal in the pilot doc.
[10:10] Markus: Are there any customers in regulated verticals doing exactly what we ask?
[10:16] Alex: Yes, we've onboarded finserv and health customers in Private with SOC2+custom KMS integrations; we can share redacted case studies.
[10:25] Sam: On monitoring — we need per-token billing visibility and traceables back to user. Can we integrate billing events into our cost center tagging?
[10:36] Priya: Yes, token-level cost breakdowns and route tags are available. For Private you can push logs with cost tags into your cost monitoring.
[10:46] Markus: Ok, timeline — our compliance review board meets 6/16. We'd like a pilot before that if possible.
[10:54] Alex: Sounds feasible — we'll aim to get the security pack and pilot proposal to you by 6/4 and the pilot recipe by 6/8.
[11:03] [Noise — marker]
[11:10] Nadia: Quick: retention SLA and breach notification timelines? We need 72-hour notification on confirmed breaches and a contact list.
[11:20] Alex: 72 hours is standard and we'll provide an incident response contact. We'll include escalation matrix in the security pack.
[11:30] Sam: Any limitations on FIPS/HSM cert levels? Our auditors ask for FIPS 140-2/3 validated HSM.
[11:38] Priya: We integrate with FIPS-validated HSMs via customer KMS; we can document the HSM models and validation.
[11:47] Leah: What about developer access to debug logs — redaction options? We can't have devs seeing raw PII.
[11:56] Priya: Role-based controls plus automated PII redaction — you can mask or hash sensitive fields at ingestion. Dev access can be scoped to sanitized logs.
[12:08] Markus: Great. Any blockers from Redwood side for egress-disabled private deployment?
[12:15] Alex: Only the initial control plane handshake and log export endpoint. We'll provide workarounds: one-time bootstrap keys via signed cert exchange.
[12:27] [Longer discussion, 12:27–25:00 summarized]
[12:30] Priya: (deep dive) Deployment checklist — VPC peering, route table entries, IAM policies, KMS key policy snippets, SCIM mapping examples, SIEM export template. We'll attach templates.
[13:10] Sam: Can I get the KMS key policy example? We need to show auditors the exact permissions.
[13:18] Priya: Yes — we have an example policy for AWS KMS granting decrypt/encrypt for the Redwood runtime principal and denying cross-account by default.
[13:29] Nadia: Legal will review DPA; will you accept a mutual NDA addendum?
[13:35] Alex: Yes, we can. We'll have legal follow up.
[13:40] Leah: On RBAC mapping — can group sync be one-way from IdP to Redwood only? We want to prevent on-platform group edits.
[13:50] Priya: SCIM can be configured to be authoritative from your IdP. Platform edits can be restricted to admin roles.
[14:00] Markus: Any known perf/regressions when using envelope encryption for heavy inference workloads? We need latency SLOs.
[14:09] Priya: There's minimal crypto overhead; at scale we recommend key-caching patterns and local HSM proxies to avoid per-request remote decrypts. Latency impact is typically single-digit ms per token generation depending on key ops. We can run a benchmark during pilot.
[14:25] Alex: We'll include a benchmark recipe that simulates your workload distribution and sequence lengths.
[14:33] Sam: Also want to capture policy for data deletion upon contract termination.
[14:39] Alex: DPA covers data deletion and return/destruction timelines — standard is 30 days to a secure delete unless otherwise specified. We'll include this in the security pack.
[14:51] [Crosstalk — brief]
[15:00] Priya: Wrap-up recap — action items: share SOC2/ISO and security deck, attach KMS policy example, pilot recipe, and deployment templates.
[15:12] Markus: That works. Nadia will review DPA; Sam will send data class matrix.
[15:20] Alex: Perfect. We'll follow up with links — security pack will include: SOC2 Type II, ISO attestation, controls matrix, subprocessors list, SBOM, KMS policy examples, SCIM mapping templates, and the pilot proposal.
[15:38] Dana: I'll own the pricing follow-up and draft of pilot commercial terms.
[15:45] Markus: Great. Thanks everyone.
[15:49] Alex: Thanks all — we'll get that to you by 6/4.
[15:54] [Call end]

References shared: https://redwood.example.com/security-pack/redwood-security-deck.pdf (to be sent), pilot-plan-template.xlsx (will be attached), KMS-policy-examples.md (will be attached)

Notes on transcription: some names/titles may be slightly off; noise on lines 3–6 caused a gap.
